Mega Matrix ( (MPU) ) just unveiled an announcement.

Mega Matrix Inc. has called an extraordinary general meeting of shareholders in Singapore for September 1, 2026, with a record date of August 20, 2026, to vote on major changes to its share capital and governing documents. The meeting will be conducted under the company’s existing multi‑class share structure, which allocates one vote per Class A share, 100 votes per Class B share and 50 votes per Class C share, with joint holders’ voting determined by seniority on the register.

Shareholders are being asked to approve a 20‑for‑1 share consolidation effective September 15, 2026, which will increase the par value of ordinary shares and substantially reduce the number of authorized shares in each ordinary class while keeping preferred shares unchanged. Conditional on that consolidation, investors will also vote on adopting a fourth amended and restated memorandum and articles of association to reflect the new capital structure, signaling a significant capital reorganization that could affect trading dynamics, liquidity and governance terms for existing stakeholders.

More about Mega Matrix

Mega Matrix Inc., a Singapore-based foreign private issuer, operates with a multi‑class share structure comprising Class A, B and C ordinary shares and preferred shares. The company is listed in the U.S. and files its reports with the Securities and Exchange Commission under Form 20‑F, reflecting a shareholder base governed by Cayman‑style memoranda and articles of association.

Its capital structure features differentiated voting rights, with Class B and Class C shares carrying significantly more votes per share than Class A shares. This architecture is designed to concentrate control among key stakeholders while maintaining broader access to equity capital through its large authorized share base and U.S. registration statements.
